question.text: Rebalancing via INFLOWS (new deposits) rather than sales is tax-efficient because:

answer.text: It avoids triggering capital gains on overweight positions

explanation.text: The Logic: Selling an overweight position to bring the portfolio back to target weights crystallises capital gains, which triggers tax. If instead the investor channels fresh deposits into the underweight buckets, the overweight positions are diluted relatively (their weight falls as the total grows) without any sale event — so no capital-gains tax is realised. The compounding base remains intact. The Trap: "No tax, period" is incorrect — capital gains taxes still apply when assets are eventually sold; inflow rebalancing only defers them. "It's illegal" and "It's forbidden" are wrong because using fresh contributions to rebalance is a standard, legitimate technique. Note: The specific mechanism — using new deposits to avoid triggering capital gains on overweight positions — is not explicitly stated in the cited NISM-Series-XXI-B workbook pages (185-186, 311, 396-397). The workbook supports the general capital-gains-on-sale framework, and the reasoning above reflects general tax-aware portfolio-management practice.
